title: Triage a food garden during drought
subcategory: Triage a food garden during drought
summary: Protect drinking water first, then concentrate limited irrigation on the crops most likely to produce useful food.
content: Protect drinking water first, then concentrate limited irrigation on the crops most likely to produce useful food. Use the steps as a conservative offline checklist, then follow current local rules, official alerts, product labels and competent agricultural or food-safety advice.
materials: clean dedicated containers or tools appropriate to the task
steps: Follow official restrictions and reserve safe drinking, cooking and hygiene water before garden irrigation.
List crops by remaining time to harvest, food value, current health and water needed to finish.
Stop new sowing and remove failed or low-value plants that consume scarce water without realistic yield.
Mulch suitable soil, shade vulnerable containers, repair leaks and water the root zone slowly during the lower-evaporation part of the day.
Record water used and harvest gained so the next planting plan fits the reliable supply.
warnings: Do not divert water from essential human or animal needs to keep every plant alive.
Salty, sewage-contaminated, fuel-contaminated or chemically contaminated water can damage soil, crops and health.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.
Using an unidentified material, water source, seed lot or crop.
Ignoring weather, local rules, product labels or signs of contamination.
alternatives: Reduce the plan to one small test batch or container.
Use a safer established water, seed, crop or food method when any critical condition is uncertain.
failure_signs: Unexpected odour, slime, mould, contamination, structural movement, uncontrolled pests, crop collapse or results that contradict the verified method.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this guide to override an emergency order, food recall, pesticide label, building restriction, water restriction or professional diagnosis.
short_term: Protect people, drinking water and uncontaminated food first; isolate the uncertain material and record what happened.
long_term: Keep a seasonal record of materials, varieties, water, weather, yields, losses and corrections.
if_method_fails: Stop scaling up, isolate the problem and return to a verified small trial or qualified local advice.
environment_notes: Adapt for Mediterranean heat, wind, drought, local frost, balcony exposure and the actual microclimate.
